classification.difficultyReason: Translate the minimum and endpoint measurements into a vertex-form model and evaluate the opposite endpoint.

content.prompt:
Over the summer, Mr Ding and his daredevil maths teacher friends want to build a bike ramp to launch themselves into a lake. He decided that the shape of the ramp would be parabolic.

The right end of the ramp should have a height of 5 metres.

The lowest point of the ramp should be 2 metres above the ground, 3 metres from the right end.

If the left end of the ramp is 7 metres from the right end, from what height should the ramp start? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Unshaded ramp and lake outlines with the original axis convention and labels. No numerical ticks, coordinates or calculated equation are displayed.
spec.mathematics: The ramp extends into negative x from its right end on the y-axis. Its concave-up upper boundary has an interior minimum above ground. The lake outline is contextual and has no specified depth.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent contextual diagram; the model and starting height remain answer-only.

answer.short: $7.33\text{ m}$. The model is $y=\dfrac{1}{3}(x+3)^2+2$; evaluate it at $x=-7$.
answer.worked:
Take the ramp's right end as $x=0$, with height $y$ in metres. The vertex is $(-3,2)$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=a(x+3)^2+2\\5&=a(0+3)^2+2\\3&=9a\\a&=\frac{1}{3}\\y&=\frac{1}{3}(x+3)^2+2\end{align*}$$

The left end is at $x=-7$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{1}{3}(-7+3)^2+2\\y&=\frac{16}{3}+2\\y&=\frac{22}{3}\\y&\approx7.33\end{align*}$$

The ramp should start at a height of $7.33\text{ m}$.
